item: Device cluster, two entries. C1: lossless separation of a shared tensor leg by an auxiliary Fourier/group tensor, retaining a dot product (M1 Prop 3.1 / Cor 3.2; M2 GROUP lemma in Behrend form); in character form lambda(T) >= e^{p_X H(q)} prod lambda(T_i)^{q_i} for every spectral point. C2: the symmetrized polynomial-multiplication profile P(a,b) = (prod_{pi in S3} lambda_pi(C(a,b)))^{1/(6t)} with its discrete growth (depends on C1).
item_type: F3 (C1, construction/lemma) + F1 (C2, defined object); one device cluster
lean_status_why: Both entries are formalized line by line from M1 and sit inside the comparator cone of complex_omega_le_nine_quarters: finiteSeparation_bound and Character.sharedFirst_tag are the C1 statements (sharedFirst_tag is a cut vertex reached by both the concavity and tripling branches), and symmetrizedProfile/convolutionProfile/ScalarProfile are C2; the M2 Behrend form of C1 (exists_modular_separation) is separately in the alpha, rectangular and 2.267 cones. Text-level reading only; per the environment note the orchestrator's comparator run on the main MatrixMultiplication config passes, which I did not run myself.
lean_gaps: The topological degeneration statement finiteSeparation_degeneratesTo (Separation/Basic.lean:306) is NOT in the 9/4 cone (text-level DAG). The cone uses the algebraic version value_separationTarget_le (explicit polynomial approximation plus interpolation). Same content, no loss of strength, but a prover library should export the character-level lemmas, not only the DegeneratesTo form.

Strassen duality is re-proved by M1's Appendix A route (exists_detecting_character; fixed point by finite approximation) and imports FixedPointTheorems.brouwer from the external harfe/fixed-point-theorems-lean4 package. exists_detecting_character is specialised to matrixClass d; asymptotic-rank targets need a version for an arbitrary tensor class (the Spectrum/* machinery is generic over TensorSemiring.rank, so this is an estimated 100-250 line generalisation).
Everything is over C. The Fourier step hard-codes IsPrimitiveRoot zeta (5*M), so a port to characteristic 5 cannot reuse it as is (no primitive (5M)-th root of unity exists in characteristic 5).

M1 form and M2 form are separate developments: the 9/4 cone uses only the M1 form (AuxiliarySeparation namespace); the alpha (0.465), rectangular (2.092) and 2.267 cones use only the M2 Behrend form (Foundation.Separation.exists_modular_separation via PrefixSeparationPolynomialStage); the all-field 2.371 cone (MatrixFields, M3) uses neither. M2's elementary CW_1 bound 9 log 3 / log 75 (about 2.29011) is not formalized (text grep finds no log 75).

C2: the growth lemma ScalarProfile.exponent_le_three_quarters is fully generic real analysis (sub-cone 44 decls / ~504 decl-lines); concavity and tripling are specific to C(a,b) (Clebsch-Gordan determinant filtration; three-sector degeneration). lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.AuxiliarySeparation.Character
lean_source.text:
/-- A normalized, additive, multiplicative, restriction-monotone tensor valuation.

Index types vary over all finite types in `Type`. No character-existence result is
included among the fields or claimed by this definition.
-/
structure Character where
  value : {X Y Z : Type} → [Fintype X] → [Fintype Y] → [Fintype Z] →
    Tensor ℂ X Y Z → ℝ
  nonneg : ∀ {X Y Z : Type} [Fintype X] [Fintype Y] [Fintype Z]
    (T : Tensor ℂ X Y Z), 0 ≤ value T
  map_zero : ∀ {X Y Z : Type} [Fintype X] [Fintype Y] [Fintype Z],
    value (0 : Tensor ℂ X Y Z) = 0
  map_one : value unitTensor = 1
  map_directSum : ∀ {ι X Y Z : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    [Fintype X] [Fintype Y] [Fintype Z] (T : ι → Tensor ℂ X Y Z),
    value (Tensor.directSum T) = ∑ i, value (T i)
  map_product : ∀ {X Y Z U V W : Type} [Fintype X] [Fintype Y] [Fintype Z]
    [Fintype U] [Fintype V] [Fintype W]
    (T : Tensor ℂ X Y Z) (S : Tensor ℂ U V W),
    value (Tensor.product T S) = value T * value S
  monotone : ∀ {X Y Z X' Y' Z' : Type}
    [Fintype X] [Fintype Y] [Fintype Z]
    [Fintype X'] [Fintype Y'] [Fintype Z']
    (T : Tensor ℂ X Y Z) (A : X' → X → ℂ)
    (B : Y' → Y → ℂ) (C : Z' → Z → ℂ),
    value (Tensor.restrict A B C T) ≤ value T
lean_source.note: Spectral-point interface (Strassen's asymptotic spectrum, normalized/additive/multiplicative/restriction-monotone). Every C1/C2 statement quantifies over it.

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.AuxiliarySeparation.sharedFirstTensor
lean_source.text:
/-- Branches sharing X, with matching and disjoint Y and Z sectors. -/
def sharedFirstTensor (B : Fin M → Tensor ℂ X Y Z) :
    Tensor ℂ X (Fin M × Y) (Fin M × Z) :=
  fun x y z => if y.1 = z.1 then B y.1 x y.2 z.2 else 0
lean_source.note: C1 input: branches B h sharing the X-leg, with matched disjoint Y/Z sectors.

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.AuxiliarySeparation.separationTarget
lean_source.text:
/-- The surviving tensor: sector labels match on all three legs, while the
additional second/third coordinates form a dot product. -/
def separationTarget (B : Fin M → Tensor ℂ X Y Z) :
    Tensor ℂ (X × Fin M) ((Fin M × Y) × Fin M) ((Fin M × Z) × Fin M) :=
  fun x y z => if x.2 = y.1.1 ∧ y.1.1 = z.1.1 ∧ y.2 = z.2 then
    B y.1.1 x.1 y.1.2 z.1.2 else 0
lean_source.note: C1 output: sector labels on all three legs plus an M-dimensional dot pairing (= direct sum of B h (x) dot pairing; separationTarget_eq_directSum, line 332).

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.AuxiliarySeparation.finiteSeparation_degeneratesTo
lean_source.text:
/-- Exact finite separation: `5M` source copies degenerate to all M branches,
each retaining an M-dimensional dot-product factor. -/
theorem finiteSeparation_degeneratesTo [Fintype X] [Fintype Y] [Fintype Z]
    (hM : 0 < M) (B : Fin M → Tensor ℂ X Y Z) :
    Tensor.DegeneratesTo
      (Tensor.directSum (fun _ : Fin (5 * M) => sharedFirstTensor B))
      (separationTarget B)
lean_source.note: M1 Prop 3.1 in its topological (closure) form. NOT in the 9/4 comparator cone (text-level DAG); the cone uses the algebraic polynomial-approximation form below.

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.AuxiliarySeparation.Character.value_separationTarget_le
lean_source.text:
/-- The separated constant tensor costs at most the character of the `5M`
source copies. This uses the explicit polynomial, not topological continuity. -/
theorem value_separationTarget_le (hM : 0 < M) (B : Fin M → Tensor ℂ X Y Z) :
    χ.value (separationTarget B) ≤
      5 * (M : ℝ) * χ.value (sharedFirstTensor B)
lean_source.note: Algebraic (interpolation) form of the 5M-copy degeneration; in the cone.

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.AuxiliarySeparation.Character.finiteSeparation_bound
lean_source.text:
/-- Exact finite character separation: the common first coordinate can be
separated at a cost of `5M`, retaining an `M`-dimensional first-leg dot factor. -/
theorem finiteSeparation_bound (hM : 0 < M) (B : Fin M → Tensor ℂ X Y Z) :
    (∑ h, χ.value (B h)) * (M : ℝ) ^ χ.pX ≤
      5 * (M : ℝ) * χ.value (sharedFirstTensor B)
lean_source.note: C1 core inequality (M1 Prop 3.1 at character level). Sub-cone 155 decls / ~1,167 decl-lines.

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.AuxiliarySeparation.Character.sharedFirst_tag
lean_source.text:
/-- The actual shared-input tensor tag inequality, including probability laws
with zero coordinates. The branch labels are disjoint on the second and third
legs, while the first coordinate is shared. -/
theorem Character.sharedFirst_tag (χ : Character)
    (q : FiniteLaw (Fin s)) (B : Fin s → Tensor ℂ X Y Z)
    (hB : ∀ a, B a ≠ 0) :
    Real.exp (χ.pX * finiteEntropy q.mass) *
        ∏ a, χ.value (B a) ^ q.mass a ≤ χ.value (sharedFirstTensor B)
lean_source.note: C1 entropy form (M1 Cor 3.2): lambda(T) >= e^{p_X H(q)} prod lambda(T_i)^{q_i}. Cut vertex of the 9/4 cone; sub-cone 216 decls / ~1,937 decl-lines.

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.AuxiliarySeparation.Character.sixfoldProduct
lean_source.text:
/-- The product of character values in the six orders of possibly different legs. -/
def sixfoldProduct (T : Tensor ℂ X Y Z) : ℝ :=
  χ.value T *
    χ.value (fun y z x => T x y z) *
    χ.value (fun z x y => T x y z) *
    χ.value (fun x z y => T x y z) *
    χ.value (fun z y x => T x y z) *
    χ.value (fun y x z => T x y z)
lean_source.note: C2 ingredient: product of the character over the six leg orders.

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.AuxiliarySeparation.ScalarProfile
lean_source.text:
/-- The scalar profile hypotheses used in Section 6. Only positive indices
carry mathematical content; the values on either coordinate axis are unused. -/
structure ScalarProfile (t : ℝ) where
  value : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ
  positive : ∀ a b : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → 1 ≤ b → 0 < value a b
  symmetric : ∀ a b : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → 1 ≤ b → value a b = value b a
  boundary : ∀ b : ℕ, 1 ≤ b → value 1 b = (b : ℝ)
  concave : ∀ a h : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → 2 ≤ h →
    value a (h - 1) + value a (h + 1) ≤ 2 * value a h
  tripling : ∀ a h : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → 1 ≤ h →
    3 * value a h ≤ value a (3 * h + a - 1)
  rank_bound : ∀ a b : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → 1 ≤ b →
    value a b ≤ ((a : ℝ) + (b : ℝ) - 1) ^ (1 / t)
lean_source.note: C2 scalar abstraction: boundary, symmetry, concavity, shifted tripling, rank bound.

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.AuxiliarySeparation.ScalarProfile.exponent_le_three_quarters
lean_source.text:
/-- Lemma 6.1: a positive symmetric profile satisfying the stated concavity,
tripling, boundary, and rank bounds has exponent at most `3/4`. -/
theorem exponent_le_three_quarters {t : ℝ} (P : ScalarProfile t) (ht : 0 < t) :
    t ≤ 3 / 4
lean_source.note: C2 growth lemma (M1 Lemma 6.1). Sub-cone 44 decls / ~504 decl-lines: pure real analysis, reusable for any profile.

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.AuxiliarySeparation.Character.exponent_sum_le_nine_quarters
lean_source.text:
/-- The three dot-product exponents of an actual character sum to at most `9/4`. -/
theorem exponent_sum_le_nine_quarters : χ.pX + χ.pY + χ.pZ ≤ 9 / 4

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.AuxiliarySeparation.exists_detecting_character
lean_source.text:
/-- Lemma 3.1: normalized, additive, multiplicative, restriction-monotone
characters detect every integer strictly below the exact-rank growth value. -/
theorem exists_detecting_character {d k : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    (hk : (k : ℝ) < (d : ℝ) ^ exactRankExponent) :
    ∃ χ : Character, (k : ℝ) ≤ χ.value (Tensor.matrixMultiplication d d d)
lean_source.note: Strassen duality (App. A fixed-point route; uses external FixedPointTheorems.brouwer). Specialised to matrixClass d; generalising to an arbitrary tensor class is needed for asymptotic-rank targets.

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.Foundation.Separation.exists_modular_separation
lean_source.text:
theorem exists_modular_separation {d Q K m : ℕ}
    (hK : (d * Q ^ 2 + 1) * K ≤ Q ^ d)
    (hm : (d * Q ^ 2 + 1) * m ≤ Q ^ d) :
    ∃ (tag : Fin K → AuxiliaryGroup d Q)
      (point : Fin K → Fin m → AuxiliaryGroup d Q),
      ∀ s s' i j,
        point s i + (tag s - point s j) = tag s' ↔ s = s' ∧ i = j
lean_source.note: M2 GROUP lemma, Behrend-sphere form (tags/points in an auxiliary abelian group). In the alpha, rectangular and 2.267 cones; not in the 9/4 or all-field cones.

lean_source.name: OAI.MatrixMultiplication.Foundation.finite_separation_identity
lean_source.text:
theorem finite_separation_identity
    (T : Tensor ℂ X Y Z) (lx : X → S) (ly : Y → S)
    (tag : S → G) (point : S → U → G)
    (hlabels : ∀ x y z, T x y z ≠ 0 → lx x = ly y)
    (hcollision : ∀ s s' i j,
      point s i + (tag s - point s j) = tag s' ↔ s = s' ∧ i = j) :
    Tensor.pullback
      (fun x : X × U => (x.1, point (lx x.1) x.2))
      (fun y : Y × U => (y.1, tag (ly y.1) - point (ly y.1) y.2))
      (fun z : Z × S => (z.1, tag z.2))
      (Tensor.product T (groupTensor G)) = separatedTensor lx T
lean_source.note: M2 separation identity T (x) groupTensor G -> separatedTensor (restriction). Text-level DAG does not place it in any comparator cone (the cones reach the Behrend form via PrefixSeparationPolynomialStage).

negative_controls.title: Universal-method barrier for CW_q (Alman 2019): omega < 2.168 from CW_q alone
negative_controls.statement: Restrict the library to CW_q tensors, unit/group tensors, the spectral infrastructure and C1 (no C(a,b), no profile, no headline), and ask for omega(C) < 2.168. Alman (CCC 2019, ToC 2021) shows the universal method applied to any CW_q cannot give omega below 2.16805.
negative_controls.why_device_must_fail: C1 on CW_q is a degeneration from CW_q^{tensor n} times a group tensor; over C the group tensor is a unit tensor after Fourier, so the irreversibility/universal-method barrier still applies (M2's 2.290 and 2.258 respect it). A prover success here would indicate a library or barrier-scope error. M1 escapes only by switching to C(a,b), whose irreversibility tends to 1.

negative_controls.title: Cap set upper bound (Ellenberg-Gijswijt)
negative_controls.statement: A subset of F_3^n with no three distinct points summing to zero has size at most 3 * 2.756^n.
negative_controls.why_device_must_fail: Slice-rank / subrank upper bounds need ONE small monotone (a spectral point or slice rank) to exist; C1 only lower-bounds every spectral point of shared-leg sums (it produces degenerations, i.e. constructions). It is also over C, and the cap-set tensor lives over F_3.
